title: Bundeswehr Recruitment 2026: Voluntary Service Guide
metaDescription: Bundeswehr recruitment 2026: the new voluntary service, about €2,600 monthly pay, the questionnaire for 18-year-olds, medical checks and how to join.
headline: Bundeswehr Recruitment 2026: How to Join

sections.title: The new military service law of 2026
sections.content:
Germany's Military Service Modernization Act took effect on 1 January 2026, fifteen years after compulsory service was suspended in 2011. The new system does not bring back general conscription: registration is mandatory for young men, but actually serving remains voluntary for now. The law can trigger a needs-based draft only if voluntary recruitment falls short of its targets.

The reform answers NATO requirements and a serious personnel gap. The Bundeswehr has about 182,000 active soldiers and roughly 49,000 reservists, but the government aims for 260,000 professional and temporary soldiers plus around 200,000 reservists by 2035, within a total strength of about 460,000.

sections.title: Who gets the letter and the questionnaire
sections.content:
From 2026, every German citizen turning 18 receives a letter from the Bundeswehr with a digital questionnaire about their willingness to serve, education, health and physical condition. Men are legally required to complete and return it, while participation is voluntary for women. The obligation first covers males born from 2008, reaching roughly 300,000 to 350,000 young people each year.

Mandatory medical examinations, the Musterung, begin on 1 July 2027 for the 2008 generation. In a declared defence emergency, the government could require all men aged 18 to 60 to serve, with women serving in civilian capacities. People born between 1993 and 2007 are not covered by the new rules unless conscription is fully reinstated.

sections.title: Voluntary service: terms and pay
sections.content:
Volunteers serve a minimum of six months, with the new voluntary service lasting six to eleven months and extensions possible up to 23 months. After a twelve-month commitment, volunteers move into the category of temporary soldiers, known as Soldaten auf Zeit, with a different contract and pay regime.

Pay is a major attraction: the new voluntary service starts at approximately €2,600 gross per month, with accommodation and some benefits covered, and temporary soldiers earn from about €2,700. Volunteers can also get help with driving licence costs, and the government aims to recruit 20,000 new volunteers in 2026.

sections.title: Career paths in the Bundeswehr
sections.content:
Beyond the voluntary service, the Bundeswehr offers careers as a temporary soldier for up to 25 years, as a career soldier, or as an officer with or without a degree, including study at a Bundeswehr university. Roles span the Army, Navy, Air Force, Cyber and Information Domain Service, and the Joint Support Service.

Applicants must be German citizens, meet the medical and fitness standards, and pass aptitude and psychological assessments. Because the phased rollout is still building capacity, candidates who express interest in the questionnaire are invited to assessments first, so responding early improves the chance of a preferred role and start date.

faqs.q: Is military service compulsory in Germany in 2026?
faqs.a: No, actually serving remains voluntary. From 2026, all 18-year-old men must complete a Bundeswehr questionnaire, and mandatory medical examinations start on 1 July 2027 for those born in 2008 or later. Only if voluntary recruitment misses its targets can the government activate a needs-based draft, which the Bundestag would have to decide.

faqs.q: How much does the Bundeswehr pay volunteers?
faqs.a: The new voluntary service pays approximately €2,600 gross per month, with accommodation and certain benefits covered by the Bundeswehr. Temporary soldiers who commit for at least twelve months earn from about €2,700 gross per month, and the pay rises slightly with rank and length of service. Help with driving licence costs is also offered.

faqs.q: How long is voluntary service in the Bundeswehr?
faqs.a: The minimum term is six months, with the new voluntary service lasting six to eleven months and extensions possible up to 23 months. After twelve months, volunteers become temporary soldiers under a different contract. Longer commitments of up to 25 years are possible for those who choose a military career.

Applicants must be German citizens and pass medical, fitness and aptitude assessments. The 2026 system first contacts citizens turning 18, but older volunteers can also apply through the Bundeswehr careers service. Women can volunteer freely, and the force recruits for the Army, Navy, Air Force, cyber service and support roles.
